clue.text: Grim place associated with Lancaster

definitions.meaning: grim here means haggard and bony, the look of someone worn thin
Ghent's old English name, carried by John, Duke of Lancaster, born there

explanation.surface: Someone describes a bleak spot linked with the Lancashire town of Lancaster.
explanation.walkthrough: John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster in Shakespeare's Richard II, took his title from Gaunt, the old English form of Ghent, where he was born.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim and gaunt both describe a haggard, bleak, emaciated appearance; the second sense is a historical place name.

clue.text: Agitated aunt eager for assurance

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters of the two words that follow are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A relative who is nervous and keen wants to be reassured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitated' rearranges AUNT EAGER into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An assurance and a guarantee are both a firm promise that something will happen or hold good.

clue.text: Total put into circulation

definitions.meaning: total as an adjective, meaning complete or absolute, as in an outright fool
to pass forged coins or notes into use, a legal sense of the verb

explanation.surface: A sum of money is released into general use.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the old legal one: to utter a forged banknote is to pass it off as genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can mean complete or absolute; the second sense is the legal term for passing counterfeit money.

clue.text: Element indirectly represented by Western leader

definitions.text: Element indirectly represented by Western leader

parts.words: Element indirectly represented by Western leader
parts.note: the chemical whose symbol is W, the first letter of Western; indirectly because the symbol comes from its other name, wolfram, not its English one

explanation.surface: A political element is only obliquely spoken for by the head of the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western leader' is W, and W is the chemical symbol of this metal, taken from its German name wolfram, which is why the representation is only indirect.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical element whose symbol W derives from the alternative name wolfram rather than the usual English name.

clue.text: Special sort of vehicle for Toad, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a craft built to travel on both land and water
a toad is an example of a creature living partly in water and partly on land

explanation.surface: A peculiar motor car is acquired for Mr Toad, the car-mad hero of The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Toad of Toad Hall, who is obsessed with motor cars; but the toad is just an example of the animal class.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a land-and-water vehicle and a cold-blooded creature like a frog or newt that lives on land and in water.

clue.text: Book used for parts of play

definitions.meaning: the book of the New Testament after the Gospels
the major divisions of a stage drama

explanation.surface: A script is used to divide up a drama into sections.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a New Testament book and the main divisions into which a drama is split.

clue.text: Differing greatly, like people in Szczecin and Katowice

definitions.meaning: an idiom for being utterly opposed in views

definitions.text: like people in Szczecin and Katowice
definitions.meaning: Szczecin is in the far north-west of Poland and Katowice in the far south, so their inhabitants are Polish people far from each other

explanation.surface: Residents of two Polish cities have very different outlooks.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the phrase describes Polish people a long way apart: Szczecin lies near the Baltic and Katowice near the southern border.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having completely opposite views, as far apart as the north and south ends of the earth.

clue.text: Such clubs aren't exclusively for Asian swingers

definitions.text: Such clubs aren't exclusively for Asian swingers

parts.words: Such clubs aren't exclusively for Asian swingers
parts.note: bottle-shaped wooden clubs swung in gymnastic exercise carry the name of a South Asian nationality, yet anyone may swing them

explanation.surface: Certain nightclubs are not reserved for fun-loving people from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Indian clubs are juggling-pin-shaped clubs swung for exercise; 'swingers' suggests partygoers, but means people swinging the clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: These exercise clubs are named after the subcontinent where the practice originated, though anyone swings them.

clue.text: One new tax worker found neverending

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
cess is an old word for a local tax or levy
the ant is the crossword's stock worker insect

explanation.surface: A fresh employee at the revenue office is found to be endlessly busy.
explanation.walkthrough: CESS is an old word for a rate or levy, still met in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unceasing never stops, so it can be called neverending.

clue.text: Fabric manufactured in US city with 50% English capital

parts.note: NY is the standard abbreviation for New York

indicators.note: fifty per cent means only half of the capital's name is kept, the second half dropped

parts.note: London is the capital of England

explanation.surface: Cloth is produced in an American city with half its money from England.
explanation.walkthrough: '50%' keeps the first half of the capital's name. 'Capital' looks like money but is the city, and 'manufactured in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic material woven into cloth for stockings and clothing.

clue.text: Advance payment African province required before delivery

parts.note: the ante is the stake put up in advance in poker
Natal was a province of South Africa, now KwaZulu-Natal

explanation.surface: A down payment is demanded by an African region before goods are delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' suggests goods, but is the birth of a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenatal care happens during pregnancy, before the birth, which is the delivery of the baby.

clue.text: Like a sovereign prince of the French state

parts.note: du is French for of the, masculine
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone resembles a ruling prince of the French nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French state' looks like France itself, but 'of the French' gives DU and 'state' alone gives CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign duke, as of a duchy, is a ruling prince, so ducal means belonging to one.

clue.text: Run in and stop

definitions.meaning: slang for take into custody, as a policeman does
to halt or check, as in checking the progress of a disease

explanation.surface: Someone dashes inside and then halts.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick a suspect is to run him in; to halt a decline is to check it.

clue.text: Booth, for example, with beastly twins inside

parts.note: two of the same beast, a donkey each time
two of the same beast, a donkey each time
in is a synonym of inside

explanation.surface: A Booth is pictured with a pair of animal twins within it.
explanation.walkthrough: John Wilkes Booth shot President Lincoln; 'Booth' looks like a stall or kiosk.
explanation.definitionFit: John Wilkes Booth was the killer of Abraham Lincoln, an example of a political murderer.

clue.text: Refuge that's needed by wrestler

definitions.meaning: a fortified place of safety
a wrestler needs a powerful grip

explanation.surface: A shelter is required by a fighter in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress or citadel is a place of refuge; read as two words it is a firm grip.

clue.text: Watch army exercise that provides up-to-date intelligence

parts.note: ticker is old slang for a watch
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone observes a military drill that gives the latest information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a verb but is a noun; TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper strip printed by a telegraph receiver with the latest share prices and news, so it delivers current information.

clue.text: Miserable fellow interrupting expression of thanks

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the man's name goes inside the word of thanks

parts.note: cheers is an informal British way of saying thank you
Les is a man's name, so a fellow

explanation.surface: An unhappy man butts in while someone is saying thank you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupting' signals the container; 'cheers' is informal British for thank you, and 'fellow' needs a man's name rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheerless lacks any joy, so it is gloomy and dreary.

clue.text: Morse's part cut for stylistic effect

definitions.meaning: the long signal in Morse code, alongside the dot
from the idiom cut a ..., to look stylish

explanation.surface: A section of Inspector Morse's role is trimmed to improve the style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morse' calls up the TV detective, but means the telegraph code; to cut a dash is to make a stylish show.
explanation.definitionFit: The long signal in Morse code, and a flourish of style or panache in the phrase cut a dash.

clue.text: There's a new Bible version inside, one gathers

indicators.note: inside means one piece is placed within the other
new tells us the letters of the words before it are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the letters of there's, the apostrophe ignored
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone learns that a fresh translation of the Bible is within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the letters to HAESTER and 'inside' places the Bible version within. 'one gathers' looks like 'I hear', but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvester is a reaper, a person or machine that brings in crops.

clue.text: Bliss for one scoring lots of runs!

definitions.meaning: Sir Arthur Bliss was an English writer of music, Master of the Queen's Music
writing music full of quick scale passages, read as a cricketer making many runs

explanation.surface: A batsman's joy at making a big score in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bliss' looks like happiness, but is Sir Arthur Bliss; 'scoring' and 'runs' suggest cricket but mean writing music with rapid scale passages.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Bliss wrote music, and a person who writes scores with runs is a writer of music.

clue.text: England as alternative for this statesman?

definitions.text: England as alternative for this statesman?

parts.words: England as alternative for this statesman?
parts.note: in Richard II John of Gaunt calls England 'this other' paradise, the garden of Genesis, which is also the surname of a British prime minister

explanation.surface: A question whether England could stand in for a particular politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaunt's speech in Shakespeare's Richard II calls England 'this other Eden', so the garden is an alternative name for England; Sir Anthony Eden was Prime Minister in 1955-57.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was a British Prime Minister and Foreign Secretary, and shares his surname with the biblical garden.

clue.text: Fine publicity surrounding our type of bed

indicators.note: surrounding means placed around, so the word our sits inside the pair before it

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
a poster is a piece of publicity
taken as written

explanation.surface: Expensive advertising wraps round one kind of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' signals the container: the pair from 'Fine publicity' goes round the word 'our'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed with a tall post at each corner, often hung with curtains.

clue.text: Surroundings of Greek character consuming single pork pie

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the Greek letter holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
I is the Roman numeral one
pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie, often shortened to porky

explanation.surface: A Greek letter swallows a solitary meat pie in its setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pork pie' is British rhyming slang (porky pie) for a lie; 'consuming' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is someone's social setting or environment.

clue.text: Coach caught replacing Middlesex opener at start of match

indicators.note: replacing means one letter takes another's place in the word for a match
at start of says the letter replaced is the first of the word for a match

parts.note: a marriage is a match between two people

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter of Middlesex, as a cricket opener goes in first

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cricket coach takes a catch when standing in for the Middlesex opening batsman at the start of play.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture is false: Middlesex, a county side, gives only M, the first letter of MARRIAGE ('match'), which C ('caught') replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a horse-drawn carriage, and also a railway carriage.

clue.text: Many noisy insects massed in flight, perhaps

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
loud is a synonym of noisy

explanation.surface: Lots of buzzing insects swarm together in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives C, the Roman hundred; the definition is the swarm, 'perhaps' showing it is one example of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm of flying insects can be called a cloud, as in a cloud of midges.

clue.text: Argue with opposing players, being thin on the ground

parts.note: spar means to argue or dispute
S and E, South and East, sit on opposing sides at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Someone quarrels with the other team, though they are few in number.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, South and East are on opposite sides, so S and E are opposing players.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sparse is thinly scattered, so scarce or few and far between.

clue.text: Inflexible oil installation I had assembled

parts.note: a rig is a platform for drilling oil
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A stiff oil platform is something I had put together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rigid is stiff and will not bend, so unbending.

clue.text: Head of chapter: A Wooded Valley

definitions.meaning: the senior clergyman presiding over a cathedral's chapter of canons
a dene, a narrow wooded valley, is also spelt this way, as in place names like Forest of this name

explanation.surface: A book's opening heads a chapter titled A Wooded Valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chapter' suggests a book chapter, but is the body of clergy running a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior priest of a cathedral heads its chapter; the same word, also spelt dene, means a narrow wooded vale.

clue.text: Daggers taken in to be licensed

indicators.note: taken in means held within, so the answer is a run of letters inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Weapons are brought inside to be given a licence.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the run inside 'tO BE LIcensed'; the daggers are printer's marks, not weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelus is the dagger-shaped mark used in printing for footnotes; this is its plural.

clue.text: Mistake concerning aid to alignment

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
a sight on a gun or telescope helps line it up with a target

explanation.surface: An error about a device for lining things up.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a slip made by failing to notice something.

clue.text: Release record, finally, with one's chorus on

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word just before it

parts.note: one's read as one is, contracted, gives I and IS run together
burden is an old word for the refrain or chorus of a song

explanation.surface: A singer issues a record which at last has their chorus on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'I's', I is, giving IS; BURDEN is an old word for a song's refrain.
explanation.definitionFit: To disburden is to relieve of a load, so to free or release.

clue.text: Haggard traveller like Cobbett

definitions.meaning: H. Haggard, author of King Solomon's Mines, had this as his first name
William Cobbett wrote Rural Rides, about his journeys on horseback round England

explanation.surface: A gaunt wayfarer resembles the radical writer William Cobbett.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like the adjective for gaunt, but is the novelist H. Rider Haggard; Cobbett wrote Rural Rides, describing his travels on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Rider Haggard was the Victorian adventure novelist, and Cobbett travelled England on horseback, as one who rides.
